<!-- pr-reviewer: 45748a1f7ed4c4360337ba55d755f2a2e6bb9007 -->
Needs changes before merge. One clippy error blocks the gate.

**What looks good**
- The change is two UI files only. No golden, no snapshot PNG, no `CHANGELOG.md` and no process file changed.
- The wear-rate check is not new. The page calls `condition_refusal` (`crates/post/src/machine/edm_conditions.rs:186`), which uses `wear_rate_ok` from the loader. A wrong wear rate (below 0, 1 or more, NaN, infinite) is named on the page and refused at Apply. The test `a_bad_wear_rate_is_named_and_refused_like_the_loader_does` pins this.
- A missing wear rate stays `None`. The code documents that the burn then has no wear compensation (`edm_conditions.rs:77`). The tick seeds 0.1, and the user must correct it. Nothing changes silently.
- The editor is sinker-only, so the wire rule "wear is a sinker field" cannot be broken here.
- The edit goes through the existing undoable `EditMachineApply`. No new command, so no MCP tool is owed.
- The hand-resolved merge (`59f4d9332`): `git show --remerge-diff` shows only the conflict in `sinker_machine_tests.rs`. The resolution keeps both sides: the two new wear tests, and main's `the_sinker_machine_editor_names_every_input` (#1119) with its assertions intact. The `NodeT` import is the only extra change. In `machine_edm_editor.rs`, `stated_num` keeps main's `Unit` signature and behaviour. It now calls `stated_with`, and `stated_plain` is the unit-less twin.

**Results merged with main (locally, main at trial-merge time, clean merge)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- sinker_machine machine_edm structural` (CWD `crates/ui`): 19 passed, 0 failed. This includes both new tests and `wire_machine_editor_structure`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: FAILED.
```
error: redundant closure
  --> crates\ui\src\egui_app\machine_edm_editor.rs:68:37
68 |     stated_with(ui, label, v, seed, |ui, x, name| fields::num_plain_named(ui, x, name));
   |   help: replace the closure with the function itself: `fields::num_plain_named`
```

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_edm_editor.rs:68`: pass `fields::num_plain_named` directly instead of the closure. Then run clippy again. The PR body says clippy passed, but it fails on the merged tree (it may be a newer toolchain lint).

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The PR body says screenshots are owed for this UI change. Please add them to the description before the maintainer merges.
- The two older Apply tests now wait 10 steps instead of 4. This is acceptable.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: a5754d5df76fa02f11c01678c47bef06017f1296 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

The earlier blocker is fixed. In `crates/ui/src/egui_app/machine_edm_editor.rs`, `stated_num` now calls `stated_with` with a closure that captures the unit `u`. That closure is needed, so `redundant_closure` no longer fires. `stated_plain` passes `fields::num_plain_named` directly.

What looks good
- The wear rate and notes edit the machine draft only. Apply uses the existing undoable `EditMachineApply`, so no new command and no MCP tool is owed.
- A bad wear rate is named on the page and refused at Apply with the same law as the loader (`wear_rate_ok`).
- The two pinning tests cover the Apply and undo path and the refusal path.
- Only two UI files changed. No dependency, process file, snapshot PNG or golden changed.

Results merged with main (locally, no Actions run)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- sinker_machine_tests machine_edm`: 9 passed, 0 failed.

Requested before merge
- None.

Notes (not blocking)
- Screenshots are owed for this UI change. The maintainer said to merge without them.
- Pixel snapshots were not run (release lane).
- The Windows-only and macOS arms were not checked. The diff has no `cfg` lines.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
